rows.speaker: أنس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Anas reports the Prophet's account of the Resurrection: after earlier prophets decline, Muhammad intercedes repeatedly, bringing groups from the Fire into Paradise; this bears on the verse's judgment and fate of sinners.
rows.anchor: عن أَنَسٍ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏"‏ يُحْبَسُ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ حَتَّى يُهِمُّوا بِذَلِكَ

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says intercession releases some from the Fire, but those whom the Qur'an has held are those for whom eternal residence is due; he identifies the promised praised station with this intercession (17:79).
rows.anchor: قَالَ قَتَادَةُ وَقَدْ سَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ ‏"‏ فَأَخْرُجُ فَأُخْرِجُهُمْ مِنَ النَّارِ وَأُدْخِلُهُمُ الْجَنَّةَ، حَتَّى مَا يَبْقَى فِي النَّارِ إِلاَّ مَنْ حَبَسَهُ الْقُرْآنُ

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the Prophet reserves his unique supplication to intercede for his community on Resurrection Day, a tradition relevant to the verse's judgment and punishment scene.
rows.anchor: أَنَّ أَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Anas reports the Prophet saying that no one in Paradise wishes to return to worldly life, even with all earth's goods, except a martyr who longs to be killed again for the honor he sees; this illustrates the verse's test through earthly adornment.
rows.anchor: سَمِعْتُ أَنَسَ بْنَ مَالِكٍ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that polytheists who had committed many murders and acts of fornication asked Muhammad whether their past deeds could be expiated; verses 25:68 and 39:53 then revealed, telling them not to despair of God's mercy.
rows.anchor: عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ـ رضى الله عنهما ـ أَنَّ نَاسًا، مِنْ أَهْلِ الشِّرْكِ كَانُوا قَدْ قَتَلُوا وَأَكْثَرُوا وَزَنَوْا وَأَكْثَرُوا،
